title: The Duke of Guastalla's letter on a "lettera reversale", 24 September 1717 (Biblioteca Estense, Autografoteca Campori, Lettera A, cc. 15-16): a two-digit number cipher read by Prabal Gupta

documents.shelfmark: Biblioteca Estense Universitaria, Modena, Autografoteca Campori, Lettera A, Antonio Ferdinando duca di Guastalla, cc. 15-16
documents.route: Antonio Ferdinando Gonzaga, Duke of Guastalla -> a correspondent who is not named

plaintext.source: The Estense record says "Lettera parzialmente cifrata" and mentions no decipherment; the contributor found no clear copy, key or draft in the folder.

transcription.source: the contributor's transcription, two passes agreeing on 92.0% of 3,064 digits with each difference settled on the scan; the project counted 3,095 digits in 556 groups in the transcription file and did not see the scan
transcription.notes: Four pages; 3 and 7 in the first digit of a pair are hard to tell apart and are written 3; clear parts in << >>.

system.summary: Letters are two-digit numbers in alphabet order from a = 30 to z = 67 (b = 25), with twins for some letters; a word may end in a single digit for its last vowel (5 a, 6 e, 7 i, 8 o, 9 u); a few short numbers stand for words (2 che, 18 non, 1 e) and about ten code groups for names and titles stay unread.

prior_solution.where: The Estense record mentions no decipherment; the contributor found none in the folder, the ledger, the catalogue searches or Affò's history of Guastalla (recipients' papers and Vienna not searched).

conditions.human_role: Prabal Gupta transcribed the letter, found the key and built the reading (issue #329, repository prabal-rje/branicki-1757). The project re-ran the decryption and a control; it has not seen the scans.

solution.what: The contributor transcribed the four pages in two passes agreeing on 92.0% of 3,064 digits, settling each difference on the scan.

Count matching and a fit on Italian letter counts found the key from this letter alone, with no other letter, key or crib; a key from the first half alone agrees with the full key on 98.3% of the second half (contributor's figure).

The decryption was read as Italian between a clear opening and closing; Trautson and Starhemberg were read as names in the cipher; about ten code groups stay unread; a blind reader named the text Italian and translated about 85% of the sense.
The contributor searched the ledger, the other 13 items in the Campori folder, two Campori catalogue searches, names and Affò's history of Guastalla vol. IV: no reading found.

Project check: the key decrypts the 1,668 letters of the cipher groups; 95.2% of them agree with the contributor's decryption; against 300 shuffled keys a word-list test gives 35.2% for the key, mean 17.7% and best 34.5% for the shuffles, a weak separation (VERIFICATION.md). No scan compared.

validation.notes: The project's n-gram test needs an Italian model of the period (lang/) and the single letter is short; a word-list test against 300 shuffled keys was used instead (VERIFICATION.md) and separates the key from the average shuffle but not clearly from the best one.

outcome.method_basis: Contributor's claim: the key was found from the ciphertext of this letter alone by count matching on Italian letter counts, with no other letter, key or crib; the project verified that the key decrypts the letter into Italian words and re-ran a weak shuffled-key control, but did not repeat the search.

credits.note: key, transcription and reading of the Guastalla letter; issue #329; repository prabal-rje/branicki-1757, CC BY 4.0

outcome.notes: Key, transcription and reading by Prabal Gupta; checked by the project against his files and a weak shuffled-key control, not against the scans. 322 of 356 cipher units read (90.4%).
outcome.fraction_read_source: Counted from reading.md: 356 units in the cipher part (words, a bracketed code group counted as one), of which 34 carry an unread code group or a [?] mark: 322 of 356 = 90.4%.

texts.label: Letter of the Duke of Guastalla, 24 September 1717 (Estense, Autografoteca Campori, cc. 15-16)
texts.summary: A letter of Antonio Ferdinando Gonzaga, Duke of Guastalla, to a correspondent not named, in the autumn of 1717: in the contributor's reading Trautson is back from his estates and Starhemberg and Trautson are expected the following week (names read in the cipher, not checked in print); the duke cannot answer until he is told whether the claim of a lettera reversale has been dropped, which he calls a tacit abdication of his rights, and he will take the land only in the form of the old investitures; the income is too small to justify a loss of rights; the clear close wishes the correspondent's son a return to health.

reading_review.note: Read the cipher part of the reading as Italian clauses: the clauses build coherent sentences with scattered holes at the unread code groups; the clear opening and closing and the names are the contributor's reading, not an edition.
